issues.text: The sample is purposive and may be skewed toward respondents already inclined to favour stringent safety norms; the field is heterogeneous and there is no mechanism to balance across safety-oriented and capability-oriented subgroups, so the results may reflect in-group consensus rather than a broad cross-section of AI researchers and practitioners.
issues.quote: there's a risk that the sample reflects the views of those already more inclined to endorse stringent safety norms

issues.text: Over 40% of respondents are affiliated with AGI labs, which may make the findings reflect an in-group consensus; the evaluator considers this an important limitation given how central the expert-consensus claim is.
issues.quote: over 40% of respondents are affiliated with AGI labs. While their views are obviously relevant, this concentration raises the possibility

issues.text: The very high agreement rates (many above 90%) raise doubts about the depth and meaningfulness of the consensus, since items are high-level and generally uncontroversial and capture agreement in principle rather than trade-offs.
issues.quote: the extremely high levels of agreement across the proposed practices - many exceeding 90% - leave open questions about the depth and meaningfulness of that consensus

issues.text: The survey does not test whether respondents would still support safety practices when they carry costs such as delayed releases or lost competitive position, so it is unclear whether agreement reflects actionable commitment or shared abstract values.
issues.quote: it's hard to know whether the strong consensus reflects genuine alignment on what should happen when safety comes at a cost, or simply shared values at a high level of abstraction

issues.text: The study does not publish any of the collected text responses, and the evaluator does not understand this choice, noting responses could have been anonymised and rephrased to share information without compromising privacy.
issues.quote: I do not fully understand the decision to not publish any of the text responses collected

issues.text: Visualisations in the appendix suggest women may show systematically higher agreement on several items, but the non-significant gender difference may reflect low statistical power given limited gender balance in the sample.
issues.quote: the methodology may lack sufficient power to fully detect these effects
